text: What is a variant, and what does it prove?
choices: The changing value the loop computes
A different version of the loop with the same result
A non-negative whole number that strictly decreases each iteration, proving the loop stops
The invariant restated for the exit condition
explanation: A non-negative integer cannot decrease forever, so the loop can only run as many times as the variant's starting value. Invariant plus variant is total correctness — the strongest thing you can say about a loop.
